full_judgment: 5. Mr Sultan Ahmed, the learned Advocate, has further submitted that the courts below, specially the lower appellate Court being the final court of fact, departing from the pleadings of the parties, have made out a third case by' basing their decision on mere presumption that the opposite parties 1-4 have acquired a title to the suit land by adverse possession in the absence of any averment in the written statement of the defendant opposite' parties and particularly in the absence of any mention .of specific date of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land. In such view of the matter, the courts below committed error of law resulting in an error in arriving at their finding and decisions causing failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decrees of the courts below are liable to be set aside. Mr Sultan Ahmed the learned Advocate for the petitioner has strongly submitted that there having been no specific and independent issues framed on the point of adverse possession of the opposite parties and there having been no specific date and year of dispossession of the plaintiff in the written statement of the said opposite parties, the unilateral finding of the lower appellate Court beyond the pleadings of the parties and in the absence of any evidence whatsoever on record, the finding of adverse possession against the plaintiff is unwarranted and is a commission of error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Lastly, it has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the judgment of the lower appellate Court having not been in accordance with the provision of Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a commission of error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and is liable to be set aside.
